wiki_title: List of human-based units of measurement

similarities.point: Both texts discuss measurement units derived from the human body.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: This is a list of units of measurement based on human body parts or the attributes and abilities of humans

similarities.point: Both texts include the cubit as a unit of measurement.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Cubit - length of the human forearm

similarities.point: Both texts include the span as a unit of measurement.
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Span - width of a human hand, from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger

similarities.point: Both texts include the palm as a unit of measurement.

differences.point: Britannica provides conversion tables for ancient units into English feet, while Wikipedia provides a descriptive list of units.
differences.quote_wikipedia: Morgen - the area that one man could plow from morning to noon

differences.point: Britannica focuses on specific regional measures like the Paris ell, while Wikipedia lists globally diverse anthropometric units.
differences.quote_britannica: cobres ten wherever are equal to three Paris ella.
differences.quote_wikipedia: A cross-cultural review of body-based measurement systems has found such units to be ubiquitous worldwide.

claims.claim: The yard is equal to 3 feet.
claims.quote_wikipedia: Ell (Scots) - length of an average person's arm

claims.claim: The pace is equal to 3 feet.
claims.quote_wikipedia: Pace - a full stride, from heel to heel

claims.claim: The digit is a unit of measurement.
claims.quote_wikipedia: Digit - length of a human finger
